title: Check yourself: checked and unchecked exceptions

questions.stem: A plugin host was compiled against version 3 of its plugin API, in which `Task.execute()` declares no exceptions. Its loop wraps each call in `try { task.execute(); } catch (RuntimeException e) { log(e); }`. A vendor builds its plugin against version 4, where `execute()` declares `throws java.sql.SQLException`, and the host loads that jar without being rebuilt. The plugin throws an SQLException. What happens?

options.text: The SQLException goes past the host's catch unchanged, since the JVM never compares a thrown exception with a throws clause
options.says: throws lives in an Exceptions attribute only javac reads; the call links by name and descriptor, so the checked exception travels on and catch (RuntimeException) doesn't match it

options.text: The SQLException goes past the host's catch as an Error, since the JVM turns a checked exception that nobody declared into an Error
options.says: the JVM passes the exception on unchanged; the stale caller's run showed the original checked exception leaving main

options.text: The host's catch logs the SQLException, since the JVM wraps a checked exception that nobody declared in an unchecked one
options.says: nothing wraps it: the stale NightlyReport run printed the original RatesUnavailableException, not a wrapper

options.text: The host's catch logs the SQLException, since at run time a catch for RuntimeException matches whatever the caller didn't declare
options.says: a catch matches by class; SQLException is not a RuntimeException, which is why the stale report's catch (RuntimeException) missed RatesUnavailableException

origin.section: Catch-or-Declare Is a Compiler Rule; at Run Time Any Method Can Throw a Checked Exception

questions.stem: A team owns `interface Exporter { void export(Report r); }`. Five classes implement it, and forty call sites call it through an `Exporter` variable. The team changes the method to `void export(Report r) throws IOException;` and rebuilds everything. Which code now fails to compile?

options.text: The five implementations, since each one must now declare IOException on its own export method
options.says: an implementation may throw less than the interface method declares; only adding a checked exception the interface lacks is an error

options.text: The five implementations and the forty call sites, since a throws clause on an interface method binds both sides
options.says: the implementations still compile: an override may declare fewer checked exceptions

options.text: The forty call sites, since each one must now catch or declare an IOException
options.says: a checked exception added to a method is unreported at every call that neither catches nor declares it; implementations may throw less

options.text: None of it, since a throws clause is checked only when an exception is actually thrown
options.says: the compiler checks catch-or-declare at every call, whether or not anything is thrown at run time

origin.section: Adding a Checked Exception Breaks Every Caller's Source; Adding an Unchecked One Breaks None

questions.stem: A workflow engine declares `class Shutdown extends Throwable` to unwind a running step quickly. A step's author wraps its whole body in `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { markFailed(e); }`, and a Shutdown is thrown inside that body. What follows?

options.text: The step is marked failed, since a catch for Exception handles every exception a method has to declare
options.says: Shutdown extends Throwable directly, so it is checked but not an Exception, and catch (Exception e) doesn't match it

options.text: The step is marked failed, since Shutdown is checked and every checked exception is an Exception
options.says: Throwable and its direct subclasses are checked without being Exceptions

options.text: Shutdown passes the catch, since a class that extends Throwable directly is unchecked like an Error
options.says: only RuntimeException, Error and their subclasses are unchecked; a direct Throwable subclass must be declared

options.text: Shutdown passes the catch, since a class that extends Throwable directly is not an Exception
options.says: catch (Exception e) matches Exception and its subclasses only, and Shutdown is a checked Throwable outside that branch

origin.section: A Throwable Is Checked Unless It Is a RuntimeException or an Error

questions.stem: `Templates.render(String name, Map<String, Object> model)` renders templates packed inside the application's own jar, and every caller passes the name as a string literal in its own code. Which kind of exception should `render` throw when no template has that name?

options.text: A checked one, since each caller should be made to deal with a template that isn't there
options.says: a caller can do nothing at run time about a name fixed in its code; the forced handler ends up empty or wrapping

options.text: A checked one, since a template missing from the jar is a condition outside the caller's code
options.says: the name comes from the caller's own code, so a missing template means the caller has a bug, like a URI constant in URI.create

options.text: An unchecked one, since the caller has nothing to do at run time except correct its code
options.says: like a URI constant passed to URI.create, a wrong bundled name is a programming error the caller can only fix in code

options.text: An unchecked one, since the JVM spends less time throwing and catching it than a checked one
options.says: at run time checked and unchecked exceptions are thrown, caught and cost the same

origin.section: Make It Checked When the Caller Can Act on It, Unchecked When It Means a Bug
